Yeah, this was very fortuitous set of circumstances this year for us to finally get that across the finish line. My father initiated that effort. It really started when he was the government teacher at South San Francisco High School. He would often Yet his kids involved in local city council meetings and school board meetings, and I think he would give them extra credit if they got involved in any particular city council campaign. He never steered them in one direction or the other and never steered them certainly from a partisan standpoint. But he really wanted to encourage young people to get involved in civic affairs and in local government in particular. Local government is where he really believes that young people could have a direct impact and they could see the impact of their efforts. So that started him thinking about what are some other ways to get young people engaged early in voting and in politics and maybe that kind of fires their interests and aspirations themselves. So he took that classroom experience when he came to the Capitol and introduced the ACA a number of times. He did it at least twice. Some of his colleagues stepped up and sort of carried that. baton forward and then I've tried it myself a couple of different times so we finally this year we're able to garner the two-thirds vote in both the assembly and the senate to put it on the ballot and what's sort of interesting it's actually a little surprising that it's been so hard for that to happen because it's already in place in 18 other states so-called red states and blue states.
